answer:
Solve a cantilever beam problem using Euler-Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic) with N-mm-MPa units throughout.
The beam is fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L, with length L = 1800 mm.
The material is structural steel with modulus of elasticity E = 200000 MPa.
The second moment of area is constant at I = 1200000 mm^4.
A downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end (x = L).
The bending moment distribution is M(x) = P(L - x), varying linearly from PL at the fixed end to 0 at the tip.
The fixed end (x = 0) has zero slope; the free end has nonzero slope and nonzero deflection.
Compute the free-end slope using the formula theta = P L^2 / (2 E I), and report the result in radians.
Compute the free-end vertical deflection using the formula delta = P L^3 / (3 E I), and report the result in mm (positive downward).
Present the final answers clearly labeled as (i) slope at free end and (ii) deflection at free end.
